text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

Before I draft this, a few questions. The email's success depends mostly on how it handles last July, so most of these are about that.

1. **Can you offer anything for last season's short boxes?** A former member's main objection will be that they got about half the produce for 6 weeks with no refund or credit and only one short email. A discount, a credit or a free week would answer that directly. If you can't offer anything, I'll write a plain acknowledgment and apology instead. Either way, it needs to be something you're willing to stand behind.
2. **If a storm hits again, what happens to members' boxes?** The new field and hail nets lower the risk. Even so, a reader will wonder whether they'd be left short again with nothing in return. If you have a policy, like credit when boxes fall below a certain level, it's your strongest answer. If you don't have one, that's fine, and I won't make one up.
3. **Do the hail nets cover only the tomatoes and peppers?** I want to describe the protection accurately without suggesting the whole farm is covered.
4. **Do you know why people left?** For example, survey replies, or comments people made when they didn't renew. If the hail wasn't the main reason, the email should lead with something else.
5. **What are the farm's name, your name for the signature, and the sign-up link or steps?** I'll need these so I don't leave blanks in the email.

1. No, I can't offer anything for last season. I just want to say sorry plainly. I didn't write more after the hail because I was working 16-hour days trying to save what was left.
2. This year we'll give a credit for any week when weather cuts a box by more than a third. I'll also send a short email to members every Thursday of the season. I can't promise there won't be any crop loss this year, though.
3. Yes, only the tomatoes and peppers. The greens aren't covered.
4. 41 of the 97 answered a short survey in the fall. 29 of them said they'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks.
5. Greenbank Farm. Sign it Sam Turner. Sign-up is through the link on our website.

I've written the email around your apology and the new credit for weather-hit weeks. Your fall survey found that how you handle bad weeks was the main thing keeping people away, so the fix comes right after the apology. It's 193 words including the subject line.

<final_document>
Subject: About last July, and what's changed

Hi,

On July 9, hail destroyed about half our crops. For six weeks, your boxes held about half of what they should have. We gave no credit, and I sent one short email. I was working 16-hour days to save what was left, but you deserved better than that, and I'm sorry.

Most of you who answered our fall survey said you'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks. Here's what we've done:

- Any week that weather cuts a box by more than a third, you get credit for it.
- I'll email all members every Thursday of the season.
- You can pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- We spent $31,000 on a second field on higher ground and hail nets over the tomatoes and peppers. The greens still aren't covered, and I can't promise a season without crop loss.

A full share is still $540, the same as last year.

We have 52 shares left, and sign-up closes March 15. If you'd like one, the link is on our website.

I hope you'll give us another season.

Sam Turner
Greenbank Farm
</final_document>

- **The 16-hour days:** I put this right before "you deserved better" so it reads as the reason you went quiet, not as an excuse.
- **The survey:** I wrote "most of you who answered" (29 of 41). It's accurate and sounds warmer than the raw numbers. Add "29 of 41" back if you'd like it to be more specific.
- **What's covered:** The email says the greens aren't under the nets and that you can't promise no crop loss. Members will see this for themselves, and it makes the new credit easier to believe.
